title: SimpRight project config
description: The project's toolchain config, read by the QA agents and the scripts (never by tests): paths, commands, ID rules, roles, API and UI exemplar files and rules, live app guardrails, the parts in use, CI facts, the test runs and the portal's text.

template.description: The version of SimpRightTemplate (a tag of Zaytsman/SimpRightTemplate) the core files match; simpright doctor compares them.

conventions.description: Files with the prose conventions, the project's own and the framework's; agents read them before writing code.

bugs.description: Bug folder: one <ID>.yml per bug in the app under test; a scenario with a knownIssue names its bug.

contracts.description: API contracts, one markdown file per area.

contractFormat.description: The contract format specification the contract writer follows.

pages.description: Page objects, with components/ and dialogs/ inside.

userStories.description: User stories, bug reports and acceptance criteria: input for the requirements analyst and the UI scenario writer.

analysis.description: Analysis documents with test plans, one per work item, written by the requirements analyst.

testData.description: Test data: shared constants and factories.

wiki.description: The wiki's pages (parts.wiki): published to the repository's GitHub wiki.

coverageSummary.description: API coverage summary; generated, so it may not exist.

ciRunInfo.description: Shows a CI run ({run}): workflow, branch, commit, time and conclusion.

ciFailedLog.description: Prints the logs of the failed steps of a CI run ({run}).

repeatSpec.description: Runs a spec several times in a row, to catch flaky tests.

validateContracts.description: Checks the contract folder against the contract format; may need an optional package.

diffContracts.description: Lists the endpoints added, removed and changed between the contracts and an OpenAPI spec ({spec}).

contractsFromOpenApi.description: Converts an OpenAPI spec ({spec}) into draft contracts.

inspectUi.description: Read-only page inspector: prints the data-test elements and accessibility tree of a page ({path}, relative to baseUrl).

ids.description: Scenario IDs are <PREFIX>-<number>, numbered across the whole layer (not per area) with a fixed number of digits; a scenario file lives in <layer>/<area>/<name>.yml.

layers.description: Layer folder name -> its ID prefix and number of digits, e.g. api: { prefix: API, digits: 4 } for API-0001.

areas.description: Area folder names under each layer, e.g. products.

bugs.description: Bug IDs: <PREFIX>-<number> with a fixed number of digits, e.g. BUG-001; the file is <paths.bugs>/<ID>.yml.

fileNames.description: Layer -> regex for scenario file names (without .yml); {area} stands for the area folder name. Layers not listed accept any kebab-case name.

roles.description: Login roles; a scenario's role must be one of these.

api.description: Optional: only projects with API tests have it.

exemplars.description: Existing files whose style new code copies.

checks.description: Shared checks for steps (status, body, errors), reused by every spec.

steps.description: Shared step helpers: send and attach, auth labels, templates for tests that differ only in data.

cleanup.description: Where the cleanup fixture is defined.

testDataUtils.description: Helpers factories use, such as unique names.

knownIssue.description: Code that marks a test as hitting a known issue; {bug} is the scenario's bug ID and {text} its knownIssue.

rules.description: Agent-critical rules only; everything else is in project.conventions.

ui.description: Optional: only projects with UI tests have it.

exemplars.description: Existing files whose style new code copies.

component.description: A reusable part of a page.

dialog.description: A dialog, or the base class dialogs extend.

fixtures.description: Where page, component, dialog and flow fixtures are registered.

preconditionFixture.description: A fixture that starts a test on a prepared page.

knownIssue.description: Code that marks a test as hitting a known issue; {bug} is the scenario's bug ID and {text} its knownIssue.

rules.description: Agent-critical rules only; everything else is in project.conventions.

liveApi.description: Guardrails for anything that calls the live app, API or UI.

writes.description: Whether agents may run tests or checks that change data on the live app (API or UI).

dangerous.description: Calls that cause lasting harm, with how to avoid it.

transient.description: Known ways the live app misbehaves for a while (re-seeds, caches, slow periods, data other visitors change), so failures can be told apart from bugs.

parts.description: The framework's optional parts and whether this project uses them.

scenarios.description: Scenario and bug files, checked by simpright-scenarios validate (@simpright/scenarios).

agents.description: The QA agents and their skills.

coverage.description: The optional API coverage reporter, or false.

package.description: The npm package the coverage loader looks for.

registry.description: Its registry, when it isn't the public npm registry.

portal.description: The Automation Portal on GitHub Pages and the pages it has, or false.

testCases.description: The Test Cases pages, built from the scenarios.

bugs.description: The Bugs page, built from the bug files.

wiki.description: The pages in paths.wiki published to the repository's GitHub wiki.

core.description: The framework's core: the files a project gets from the template and keeps generic. A core code file imports only other core files, the seams and packages; simpright doctor checks it.

files.description: The core files, as repository paths: code, and documents such as the framework's conventions.

seams.description: The project's own files that the core imports (its roles and its project file), as repository paths: they may import the app's code.

ci.description: Facts about the GitHub Actions workflows: simpright apply writes the CI part's workflows from them, and simpright doctor checks them against .github/workflows/, the kit's actions and the local actions in .github/actions/.

default.description: The protected branch: scheduled runs, publishing.

work.description: The branch work happens on, when it isn't the default one.

node.description: The Node.js major version every actions/setup-node step uses, in a workflow or in a local action (through an input, as each workflow that uses the action passes it).

secrets.description: Names of the repository secrets the tests read, never their values. The reusable test workflow declares exactly these, and its callers pass them by name.

runs.description: The test runs: one report family on GitHub Pages each, run by one caller of .github/workflows/playwright-run.yml. simpright apply writes the callers; simpright doctor checks every caller against its entry.

id.description: The report family: its folder on GitHub Pages and its workflow's family input.

label.description: The name the portal shows; simpright apply also names the run's workflow after it.

workflow.description: The file name of the run's caller in .github/workflows/ (default: <id>.yml). Keep it once the workflow has run: GitHub numbers a workflow's runs per file, and the portal keeps a family's highest run numbers.

note.description: The line under the label in the portal's side panel.

project.description: The Playwright project, or all for both in one run.

schedule.description: A cron in UTC. Without one, the run is started by hand only; every run can be.

grep.description: Runs only the tests whose title or tags match, such as @smoke.

paths.description: Space-separated spec folders or files the run is limited to, such as tests/ui/products/.

areaPicker.description: A manual run with an area input: all, or one folder of the project's tests (instead of paths).

keep.description: How many runs of the family stay on GitHub Pages.

trend.description: The layer whose health card, trends, known issues and Bugs page status this run feeds; one run per layer.

publishCoverage.description: Publishes the run's API coverage as the latest coverage report.

portal.description: The Automation Portal's text and health thresholds: the dashboard reads them from portal.json (written on every publish), the Test Cases and Bugs pages from their data files.

title.description: The brand name on the portal pages and in their titles.

titleAccent.description: The end of the title shown in the accent color, such as Right in SimpRight.

tagline.description: The line under the brand name.

description.description: The sentence at the bottom of the side panel.

healthThreshold.description: Layer -> failure rate in percent below which its latest regression counts as healthy; one per run with a trend.
